newsitem.title: GERMANY: Regulations hamper Germany's scientists - official.
newsitem.headline: Regulations hamper Germany's scientists - official.

text.p: Strict government regulations have hampered innovations in science in Germany and will continue to force companies to conduct research abroad, a senior German scientist said on Monday.
Hans-Juergen Quadbeck-Seger, a management board member at BASF AG, one of Germany's three largest chemical companies, told the daily Die Welt, "We suffer greatly from overregulation (in Germany)."
Noting that German researchers must seek approval for every single scientific test conducted on animals, Quadbeck-Seger said, "this kind of bureaucracy costs money and time."
He added "there is a trend that bio-sciences will continue to be built up more strongly abroad."
Quadbeck-Seger appealed to policy makers to alter laws and allow Germany to be more competitive.
Similarly Quadbeck-Seger also said that Germany's status as a research and production centre was hampered by high wage costs, relatively short working hours and long vacations.
Despite all of these issues however, Quadbeck-Seger said that Germany and Europe would continue to be an important market.
